name: Pookie LMS
author: Sovlix

sections.description:
Pookie LMS is a complete learning management system for WordPress. Build courses with a drag and drop builder, write lessons in the block editor, add quizzes and certificates, and let students enroll free or pay online or offline. Everything runs on your own site with no platform fees.

Why Pookie LMS

  • Move in without risk. Import from Tutor LMS, LearnPress, LearnDash, LifterLMS, MasterStudy or Masteriyo. Every import starts with a dry run and can be undone.
  • Accessible and private. Keyboard-first builder and player, WCAG AA contrast, right-to-left layouts, no telemetry.

Features

  • Course builder: sections, lessons, quizzes, drip, prerequisites, publish checklist, scheduling and review queue.
  • Quizzes: six question types, question bank, timers, attempt limits and manual grading.
  • Certificates with a public verification page, PDF download and QR code.
  • Sell courses: free, offline, Stripe, PayPal, Razorpay and Mollie; coupons, sale prices, seat limits, orders, refunds and invoices; optional WooCommerce bridge.
  • Optional Google Meet links and AI course drafting (your own API key).
  • Instructors with revenue sharing; student management with CSV; messages, reviews; reports with CSV export.
  • Integrations: blocks, shortcodes, Elementor widgets, signed webhooks, REST API, WP-CLI, optional CRM sync (Brevo, FluentCRM), GamiPress and hooks.

Privacy Policy

Pookie LMS sends no data to Sovlix (the plugin author) or any server it controls. No tracking, telemetry or advertising.

All data stays on your site, in the WordPress database and the protected uploads/pookie-lms folder (quiz answer files); card and account details never reach your site, and the audit log stores only a one-way hash of IP addresses. Pookie LMS supports Export and Erase Personal Data, adds suggested text to Settings > Privacy, and sets only the one small cookie listed in the FAQ, with no personal data. Outside services are contacted only after an administrator turns on the feature that needs them; see External services.

Sovlix Privacy Policy: https://sovlix.com/privacy-policy/
Sovlix Terms of Service: https://sovlix.com/terms-of-service/

External services

No outside service is contacted out of the box: no telemetry and no CDN fonts or scripts. The services below are used only when the feature that needs them is turned on.

YouTube video player

Used when a video is a YouTube link. The youtube-nocookie.com player is embedded; your server makes no request.

  • Purpose: playing the video and measuring watch time.
  • Data sent from the visitor’s browser to YouTube (Google): IP address, browser details, video id and referrer page address.
  • When: only after the student presses play. In the course builder, when an editor adds the link, the editor’s browser also loads the player once, hidden and muted, to read the video length.
  • Terms: https://www.youtube.com/t/terms ; Privacy: https://policies.google.com/privacy

Vimeo and other video hosts (Wistia, Loom, Dailymotion, Vidyard, Streamable)

Used when an instructor pastes a link from one of these hosts. The host’s embed page is shown in an iframe (Do Not Track on for Vimeo); your server makes no request. The list can be changed with the poklms_video_embed_hosts filter.

  • Purpose: playing the video and, for Vimeo, watch time.
  • Data sent from the visitor’s browser to the host: IP address, browser details, video id, referrer page address and any cookies the player sets.
  • When: only after the student presses play. For Vimeo links, the course builder also loads the player once, hidden and muted, in the editor’s browser when the link is added, to read the video length.
  • Vimeo: Terms https://vimeo.com/terms ; Privacy https://vimeo.com/privacy
  • Wistia: Terms https://wistia.com/terms ; Privacy https://wistia.com/privacy
  • Loom: Terms https://www.loom.com/terms ; Privacy https://www.loom.com/privacy-policy
  • Dailymotion: Terms https://legal.dailymotion.com/en/terms-of-use ; Privacy https://legal.dailymotion.com/en/privacy-policy
  • Vidyard: Terms https://www.vidyard.com/terms/ ; Privacy https://www.vidyard.com/privacy/
  • Streamable: Terms https://streamable.com/terms ; Privacy https://streamable.com/privacy

Zoom and Google Meet links

Used when an instructor adds a Zoom or Meet address to a live lesson. It is shown as a plain link that opens in a new tab; your server and the page make no request. After a student clicks it, Zoom or Google receives the usual browser data and their own terms apply: Zoom https://explore.zoom.us/en/terms/ ; https://explore.zoom.us/en/privacy/ , Google https://policies.google.com/terms ; https://policies.google.com/privacy

Video files linked by address

Used when an instructor enters the address of an MP4, WebM or HLS video on another server. On play, that server receives the IP address, browser details and referrer. When an editor adds the address in the course builder, the editor’s browser also loads the file’s first bytes once to read the video length. Its own terms and privacy policy apply.

Gravatar (profile photos)

Used when Settings > Discussion > Show Avatars is on and a page shows instructors or account details.

  • Purpose: showing a profile photo.
  • Data sent from the visitor’s browser to gravatar.com (Automattic): IP address, browser details and a hash of the person’s email address.
  • When: each time such a page is viewed.
  • Terms: https://wordpress.com/tos/ ; Privacy: https://automattic.com/privacy/

Outgoing webhooks you add

Used only after an administrator adds an endpoint in Settings > Integrations; there is no built-in endpoint.

  • Purpose: telling a system you choose that something happened.
  • Data sent from your server as a signed JSON POST: the event name (for example order.paid), a delivery id, the time, your site address, and event facts: student id, name and email, and course, order, enrollment, quiz attempt or certificate details. No passwords or card data.
  • When: after each event and on the test button; failed deliveries are retried up to 6 times. Only https addresses are allowed.
  • Terms and privacy: those of the service you choose.

Stripe (card payments)

Used only after an administrator turns on Stripe in Settings > Payments and saves a Stripe secret key.

  • Purpose: card payments on Stripe’s hosted Checkout page, refunds, and payment and dispute status. Card details never reach your site; no Stripe script is loaded.
  • Data sent from your server to api.stripe.com: order amount and currency, course title, order number, the buyer’s email address, return addresses and a site identifier; for refunds, the payment reference and amount.
  • When: when a buyer chooses card payment or returns, when an administrator refunds or checks the key, and hourly for unpaid orders. Signed webhooks arrive at /wp-json/poklms/v1/gateways/stripe/webhook and are verified.
  • Terms: https://stripe.com/legal/ssa ; Privacy: https://stripe.com/privacy

PayPal (PayPal payments)

Used only after an administrator turns on PayPal in Settings > Payments and saves a PayPal client ID and secret.

  • Purpose: payments on PayPal’s hosted page, capture, refunds, status and webhook verification. Account and card details never reach your site; no PayPal script is loaded.
  • Data sent from your server to api-m.paypal.com (api-m.sandbox.paypal.com in sandbox mode): your client ID and secret, order amount and currency, course title, order number, buyer’s email address, site name, return addresses and a site identifier; for refunds, the payment reference and amount; for webhook checks, the signature headers and event.
  • When: when a buyer chooses PayPal or returns, when an administrator refunds or tests the connection, and hourly for unpaid orders. Webhooks arrive at /wp-json/poklms/v1/gateways/paypal/webhook and are verified.
  • Terms: https://www.paypal.com/webapps/mpp/ua/useragreement-full ; Privacy: https://www.paypal.com/myaccount/privacy/privacyhub

Razorpay (Razorpay payments)

Used only after an administrator turns on Razorpay in Settings > Payments and saves a key ID and secret.

  • Purpose: payments on Razorpay’s hosted page, status, refunds and webhook verification. Card details never reach your site; no Razorpay script is loaded.
  • Data sent from your server to api.razorpay.com: your key ID and secret, order amount and currency, course title, order number, buyer’s email address, return address and a site identifier; for refunds, the payment reference and amount.
  • When: when a buyer chooses Razorpay or returns, and when an administrator refunds or tests. Signed webhooks arrive at /wp-json/poklms/v1/gateways/razorpay/webhook.
  • Terms: https://razorpay.com/terms/ ; Privacy: https://razorpay.com/privacy/

Mollie (Mollie payments)

Used only after an administrator turns on Mollie in Settings > Payments and saves an API key.

  • Purpose: payments on Mollie’s hosted page, status and refunds. Card details never reach your site; no Mollie script is loaded.
  • Data sent from your server to api.mollie.com: your API key, order amount and currency, course title, order number, return and webhook addresses and a site identifier; for refunds, the payment reference and amount.
  • When: when a buyer chooses Mollie or returns, when Mollie calls the webhook (/wp-json/poklms/v1/gateways/mollie/webhook, which carries only a payment id that is always re-fetched from Mollie), and when an administrator refunds.
  • Terms: https://www.mollie.com/en/legal/user-agreement ; Privacy: https://www.mollie.com/en/legal/privacy

Google (Meet links for live lessons)

Used only after the owner turns on Google Meet links and connects a Google account in Settings > Google.

  • Purpose: creating a Google Calendar event with a Meet room for a live lesson.
  • Data sent: the owner’s browser goes to accounts.google.com to approve Calendar access; your server sends the OAuth client ID, secret and code or refresh token to oauth2.googleapis.com/token, and the lesson title, start and end time and access token to www.googleapis.com/calendar/v3. Credentials are stored encrypted.
  • When: at connect time, when a token expires, and when an editor presses “Create Meet link”.
  • The [poklms_classroom_share] shortcode only prints a classroom.google.com/share link; Google gets the course address only if a visitor clicks it.
  • Terms: https://policies.google.com/terms ; Privacy: https://policies.google.com/privacy

AI provider (Anthropic or an OpenAI-compatible service)

Used only after the owner turns on “Enable AI features” in Settings > AI and saves an API key; the learner “Ask AI” toggle is separate. Both are off by default.

  • Purpose: drafting course outlines and quiz questions, and an “Ask AI” panel for learners.
  • Data sent from your server to the provider the owner chose: api.anthropic.com/v1/messages, or the https base URL the owner enters (by default api.openai.com/v1 for OpenAI). Sent: the API key as a header, model name, an instruction, and the editor’s topic or lesson text, or the learner’s question (up to 500 characters) with a lesson excerpt and course title. No name, email or user id is sent; nothing is stored.
  • When: once per use. Two limits protect your API budget: the monthly request limit you set in Settings > AI, and 30 requests per user per day (change it with the poklms_ai_user_daily_cap filter).
  • Anthropic: Terms https://www.anthropic.com/legal/commercial-terms ; Privacy https://www.anthropic.com/legal/privacy
  • OpenAI (default): Terms https://openai.com/policies/terms-of-use ; Privacy https://openai.com/policies/privacy-policy
  • Other providers: their own terms and privacy policy.

Brevo (contact sync)

Used only after an administrator turns on Brevo sync in Settings > CRM sync and saves a Brevo API key. FluentCRM sync calls FluentCRM’s PHP functions on your own site and makes no remote request.

  • Purpose: adding students who agreed to marketing email to your Brevo lists, unsubscribing them on withdrawn consent, and deleting them on erasure.
  • Data sent from your server to the Brevo contacts endpoint (api.brevo.com/v3/contacts) with the student’s email address, first and last name and the Brevo list ids you chose; your API key in a header. On erase, a DELETE request for the email address; on withdrawn consent, a request marking the contact as blacklisted.
  • When: queued after a consenting student enrolls, completes or buys a course or starts a membership. Nothing is sent unless the toggle is on, a key is saved and the student ticked the marketing consent box.
  • Terms: https://www.brevo.com/legal/termsofuse/ ; Privacy: https://www.brevo.com/legal/privacypolicy/

Requests to your own site

The bundled Action Scheduler sends a request from your server to your own admin-ajax.php. The Stripe “test webhook” button posts a signed test event to your own site’s Stripe webhook address. No data leaves your server in either case.

Links to outside pages

Some admin screens show plain links to the Stripe and PayPal dashboards (to copy keys) and WordPress.org. Your server makes no request and nothing is sent unless an administrator clicks a link.

Share links (X, Facebook, LinkedIn, WhatsApp)

The course page share block shows plain links to these services. Your server makes no request; nothing is sent unless a visitor clicks a link.

  • Purpose: letting a visitor share a course.
  • Data sent when a visitor clicks: the course title and address, to the chosen service.
  • Terms and privacy: https://x.com/en/tos , https://x.com/en/privacy ; https://www.facebook.com/terms.php , https://www.facebook.com/privacy/policy ; https://www.linkedin.com/legal/user-agreement , https://www.linkedin.com/legal/privacy-policy ; https://www.whatsapp.com/legal/terms-of-service , https://www.whatsapp.com/legal/privacy-policy

Images in imported content

Only when an import runs with “sideload media” on (off by default), WordPress downloads the images referenced in imported lessons.

Third-party libraries

All bundled libraries are GPL-compatible and load nothing remotely.

  • Action Scheduler 4.2.0 (GPLv3 or later) in vendor/: background tasks. Source: https://actionscheduler.org
  • mPDF 8.3.1 (GPL-2.0-only) in vendor/prefixed/mpdf: builds the certificate PDF on your server. Its DejaVu (Bitstream Vera / DejaVu font licence, free and GPL-compatible), GNU FreeFont (GPL-3.0 with font exception), XB Riyaz (GPL) and Garuda (Thai Linux Working Group, GPL-2.0 with font exception) fonts ship in ttfonts, reduced to the writing systems the certificate PDF uses (layout features kept, screen hinting removed), as their licences allow. Source: https://github.com/mpdf/mpdf
  • chillerlan/php-qrcode 5 (MIT or Apache-2.0): draws the certificate QR code. Source: https://github.com/chillerlan/php-qrcode
  • setasign/fpdi 2, psr/log, psr/http-message, myclabs/deep-copy and paragonie/random_compat (MIT): used by mPDF; prefixed with Strauss.
  • dnd-kit 6.3.1 (MIT): curriculum drag and drop, compiled into build/. Source: https://dndkit.com
  • TanStack Query 5 (MIT): data fetching, compiled into build/. Source: https://tanstack.com/query
  • Tailwind CSS 4 (MIT): only the generated CSS ships. Source: https://tailwindcss.com
  • Inter variable font (SIL OFL 1.1): local .woff2 files in assets/fonts (licence text next to them). Source: https://rsms.me/inter/
  • Lucide icons (ISC): icon outlines drawn as inline SVG in the admin app and learner pages. Source: https://lucide.dev

React, ReactDOM and @wordpress/* are not bundled; WordPress provides them.

Source code

This plugin ships its full, human-readable source code. Nothing is obfuscated.

  • PHP: src/ and templates/ (unminified).
  • Admin app, learner app and blocks: the original React and TypeScript source is in client/ (with Tailwind CSS). The files in build/ are compiled from client/ with @wordpress/scripts (webpack).
  • Build: npm install, then npm run build. JavaScript dependencies are listed in package.json; PHP dependencies in composer.json (composer install --no-dev).
  • vendor/prefixed/ holds the readable PHP source of mPDF and the QR code library exactly as published, with only their namespaces prefixed by Strauss to avoid conflicts with other plugins. Strauss source: https://github.com/BrianHenryIE/strauss
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate Pookie LMS from Plugins > Add New, or upload the pookie-lms folder to /wp-content/plugins/.
  2. Open Pookie LMS in the admin menu; the setup guide creates the catalog, student dashboard and checkout pages.
  3. Create your first course under Courses.
  4. To sell courses, turn on a payment method in Settings > Payments.
sections.faq:
Is Pookie LMS free?

Yes. Every feature described here is included and works on your own site, with no account to create and no time limit.

Can I sell courses with Pookie LMS?

Yes: free, offline, Stripe, PayPal, Razorpay or Mollie, with coupons, sale prices and seat limits. Pookie LMS takes no fee; the gateway charges its usual fees.

Can several instructors sell courses?

Yes. Instructors get a front-end area for courses, students and earnings; you set the revenue share.

Can I import from another LMS, and can I undo it?

Yes, from the LMS plugins listed above. Run a dry run first; an import can be undone from its job. The “sideload media” option (off by default) downloads images; without it no import makes a remote request.

Does Pookie LMS send data to external services?

Not out of the box. Stripe, PayPal, Razorpay, Mollie, Google, the AI provider (Anthropic or an OpenAI-compatible service) and Brevo are each opt-in and off by default: contacted only after an administrator turns the feature on and saves the keys, for the purposes listed under External services. A video host is contacted by the visitor’s browser only after a student presses play (and by the editor’s browser once, when a video link is added in the course builder, to read its length); avatars load from Gravatar only while Show Avatars is on.

Does Pookie LMS set cookies?

Besides the standard WordPress login cookies, it sets one small cookie with no personal data:

  • poklms_li (value 1) while a user is logged in, so course pages load personal progress. It ends with the login session.

Does Pookie LMS support personal data export and erasure?

Yes. Erasure deletes enrollments, progress, quiz attempts, certificates, consent, and synced Brevo and FluentCRM contacts. Orders are kept for accounting with name, email and account link removed.

Is my data removed when I delete the plugin?

Only if you turn on “Delete all Pookie LMS data when the plugin is deleted” in Settings > General (off by default).

  • When: once per use. Two limits protect your API budget: the monthly request limit you set in Settings > AI, and 30 requests per user per day (change it with the poklms_ai_user_daily_cap filter).
  • Anthropic: Terms https://www.anthropic.com/legal/commercial-terms ; Privacy https://www.anthropic.com/legal/privacy
  • OpenAI (default): Terms https://openai.com/policies/terms-of-use ; Privacy https://openai.com/policies/privacy-policy
  • Other providers: their own terms and privacy policy.

Brevo (contact sync)

Used only after an administrator turns on Brevo sync in Settings > CRM sync and saves a Brevo API key. FluentCRM sync calls FluentCRM’s PHP functions on your own site and makes no remote request.

  • Purpose: adding students who agreed to marketing email to your Brevo lists, unsubscribing them on withdrawn consent, and deleting them on erasure.
  • Data sent from your server to the Brevo contacts endpoint (api.brevo.com/v3/contacts) with the student’s email address, first and last name and the Brevo list ids you chose; your API key in a header. On erase, a DELETE request for the email address; on withdrawn consent, a request marking the contact as blacklisted.
  • When: queued after a consenting student enrolls, completes or buys a course or starts a membership. Nothing is sent unless the toggle is on, a key is saved and the student ticked the marketing consent box.
  • Terms: https://www.brevo.com/legal/termsofuse/ ; Privacy: https://www.brevo.com/legal/privacypolicy/

Requests to your own site

The bundled Action Scheduler sends a request from your server to your own admin-ajax.php. The Stripe “test webhook” button posts a signed test event to your own site’s Stripe webhook address. No data leaves your server in either case.

Links to outside pages

Some admin screens show plain links to the Stripe and PayPal dashboards (to copy keys) and WordPress.org. Your server makes no request and nothing is sent unless an administrator clicks a link.

Share links (X, Facebook, LinkedIn, WhatsApp)

The course page share block shows plain links to these services. Your server makes no request; nothing is sent unless a visitor clicks a link.

  • Purpose: letting a visitor share a course.
  • Data sent when a visitor clicks: the course title and address, to the chosen service.
  • Terms and privacy: https://x.com/en/tos , https://x.com/en/privacy ; https://www.facebook.com/terms.php , https://www.facebook.com/privacy/policy ; https://www.linkedin.com/legal/user-agreement , https://www.linkedin.com/legal/privacy-policy ; https://www.whatsapp.com/legal/terms-of-service , https://www.whatsapp.com/legal/privacy-policy

Images in imported content

Only when an import runs with “sideload media” on (off by default), WordPress downloads the images referenced in imported lessons.

Third-party libraries

All bundled libraries are GPL-compatible and load nothing remotely.

  • Action Scheduler 4.2.0 (GPLv3 or later) in vendor/: background tasks. Source: https://actionscheduler.org
  • mPDF 8.3.1 (GPL-2.0-only) in vendor/prefixed/mpdf: builds the certificate PDF on your server. Its DejaVu (Bitstream Vera / DejaVu font licence, free and GPL-compatible), GNU FreeFont (GPL-3.0 with font exception), XB Riyaz (GPL) and Garuda (Thai Linux Working Group, GPL-2.0 with font exception) fonts ship in ttfonts, reduced to the writing systems the certificate PDF uses (layout features kept, screen hinting removed), as their licences allow. Source: https://github.com/mpdf/mpdf
  • chillerlan/php-qrcode 5 (MIT or Apache-2.0): draws the certificate QR code. Source: https://github.com/chillerlan/php-qrcode
  • setasign/fpdi 2, psr/log, psr/http-message, myclabs/deep-copy and paragonie/random_compat (MIT): used by mPDF; prefixed with Strauss.
  • dnd-kit 6.3.1 (MIT): curriculum drag and drop, compiled into build/. Source: https://dndkit.com
  • TanStack Query 5 (MIT): data fetching, compiled into build/. Source: https://tanstack.com/query
  • Tailwind CSS 4 (MIT): only the generated CSS ships. Source: https://tailwindcss.com
  • Inter variable font (SIL OFL 1.1): local .woff2 files in assets/fonts (licence text next to them). Source: https://rsms.me/inter/
  • Lucide icons (ISC): icon outlines drawn as inline SVG in the admin app and learner pages. Source: https://lucide.dev

React, ReactDOM and @wordpress/* are not bundled; WordPress provides them.

Source code

This plugin ships its full, human-readable source code. Nothing is obfuscated.

  • PHP: src/ and templates/ (unminified).
  • Admin app, learner app and blocks: the original React and TypeScript source is in client/ (with Tailwind CSS). The files in build/ are compiled from client/ with @wordpress/scripts (webpack).
  • Build: npm install, then npm run build. JavaScript dependencies are listed in package.json; PHP dependencies in composer.json (composer install --no-dev).
  • vendor/prefixed/ holds the readable PHP source of mPDF and the QR code library exactly as published, with only their namespaces prefixed by Strauss to avoid conflicts with other plugins. Strauss source: https://github.com/BrianHenryIE/strauss
